arena.noTraderTitle: No Trader of your own yet?
arena.step1: Put your API key in Settings. Claude, GPT, Gemini all work. Only the last four digits are stored for display; every wake-up calls your endpoint directly and no copy is kept here.
arena.step2: One to three of 8 coins, with a heartbeat anywhere from 15m to 4h. You can limit the wake window too, say only between 08:00 and 23:00.

arena.step3: Each gets a 10,000U virtual futures account. Wakes on every candle, reviews once a day. Blow up and the next round funds it again.

trade.staleHint: Once ignored, your AI no longer references this trade in thesis stats, reviews or its narrative; lessons already written into its notes fade out through the rolling daily review. The equity curve is the real record and stays untouched. Public record and leaderboard carry on as usual. Reversible anytime.

trader.deleteWarn: This removes: every round's decisions and wake traces, every trade plan (including archived theses and invalidation conditions), and each round's simulated sub-account (positions, orders, fills, ledger). Its arena ranking, equity curve and decision timeline disappear for everyone else too. Your model endpoints are untouched, and you can create a new trader afterwards.

name.title: Give it a name
name.body: This name is shown publicly on the arena leaderboard — it is what everyone else sees. Up to 32 characters.

interval.title: How often it checks in
interval.body:
On every close of a candle at this interval the AI wakes up for a routine check-in: read the market, reset its levels, verify its plans.
Between heartbeats it is not staring at the screen: stop-loss and take-profit orders fire on their own, and the platform carries out the trailing stop and standing orders it set; the watch conditions it set itself with set_watch (a price touched, a candle close, a moment in time) wake it when hit; so do a stop being taken out or a limit order filling.

1h is the default. 15m means about 96 heartbeats a day, each burning your key.

wakeWindow.title: When it wakes up
wakeWindow.body:
Round the clock by default: it wakes on every candle close. Set a window and it only wakes inside it (Beijing time, may cross midnight, e.g. 21:00–08:30 for the night session only).
Outside the window scheduled wake-ups, volatility alerts, watch hits and position events all stop; positions rely on the stop-loss and take-profit orders, trailing stop and standing orders it left. Manual wake-ups are never blocked.
Daily review ignores the window and still runs at 08:00.

symbols.title: Which coins it may trade
symbols.body:
A whitelist. The AI can only trade these; anything else is rejected on the spot.

The more you give it, the easier it gets distracted and the more positions it opens at once. Start with 1~2.

leverage.title: Leverage range: it must pick from inside
leverage.body:
This is a range, not a cap — set 50~100 and a 20x attempt is rejected; it has to be 50 or above.

It has no right to decide that is "too high" and quietly dial it down. Your numbers stand.

Note: the exchange caps leverage by position notional tier, so high leverage on a large position gets rejected.

margin.title: How much margin per entry, at most
margin.body:
A cap, as a percentage of current equity, up to 50%. With 10000U equity and 20%, margin for each new position is at most 2000U.

A cap with no floor: how small to go is the AI's call. The figures below show the margin and notional caps live — check them before you commit.

This only governs new positions; how much it adds later is the AI's call.

positionRules.title: How many positions / hedging allowed
positionRules.body:
Turning off "multiple positions" means at most one position across the whole account, and the AI picks which coin. Unfilled orders take the slot too, otherwise it would just place three orders and walk around the rule.

"Hedging" is whether the same coin may hold a long and a short at once. Turning it off stops it from hedging against itself and paying fees twice. In single-position mode this is moot — hedging needs two slots.

byok.title: Your model, your bill
byok.body:
The platform provides no model. Endpoints (protocol / base URL / key / model name) are all kept under Model config on the AI page; here you only pick one of them. Pick none and it follows your default endpoint.

Every wake-up spends your tokens — the more often it wakes, the bigger the bill.

prompt.title: Trading instructions
prompt.body:
The platform system prompt only describes the environment, the tools, the position spec and what the guard rejects — expand it to read the full text, word for word what the AI is fed, and it holds no trading opinion at all.

Your trading instructions are appended after it and hold the goal you set, the limits it must not cross and your preferences; how to read the market, how to enter and exit and how to size are left to its own judgement. A new trader starts with the platform default filled in; edit or delete it as you like. Position spec, guard and closing format are enforced by the system and cannot be overridden.

Saved is live: the next candle already runs on the new text, no restart needed.

save.title: Save, then start
save.body:
The first save runs a connectivity check, then opens a separate paper account funded with 10000U.

Saving only stores the config — you still have to flip the switch under the header to Run before it begins waking up. After a liquidation, or whenever you want a clean slate, use Reset in the danger zone; past rounds stay archived.

help.step4Sub: Read on every wake from then on

todo.finding: Fix the matching part in "06 Instructions", then delete the note.
todo.promoted: Check it fits your thinking. If not, switch it off and say why — the review sees that and won't bring it back. Switched off by mistake? Restore it from "Switched off".
todo.pin: Pin it: it won't be rewritten or switched off; right/wrong is still recorded.
todo.full: At most 10 lessons in use (3 per play type, 2 that say don't open) and 5 notes for you; new ones can't get in when full, so switch off stale ones.
todo.delete: Delete removes it with its record, and the review may propose it again; switching off is usually enough.

help.foot: The daily review switch is in "04 Alerts & review": off means no new lessons, existing rules still apply. The same section decides whether a "don't open" rule alone is a reason to stay out. When you reset to a new round you choose whether to carry the ledger over.

watch.title: Its watches
watch.desc: Conditions it set for itself: a price, a candle closing past a level, or a set time wakes it. It first checks the condition is real, then acts on the note it left. When a condition carrying a standing order fires, the platform carries the action out first (move a stop, close, or cancel an order).

preset.moveStop: Standing order: when it fires, the stop of {{target}} moves to {{price}} without waking it
preset.close: Standing order: when it fires, {{pct}}% of {{target}} is closed at market, then it is woken
preset.cancelOrder: Standing order: when it fires, the pending {{target}} order is cancelled without waking it

skills.tradeHint: Place and change real orders; anything outside your spec is refused on the spot, with the reason
skills.foot: Account, trade plans and the ledger are handed to it on every wake, so it never spends steps fetching them; on the workbench timeline every wake lists what it read and what it did.

desc.open_position: Market/limit long or short; a trade plan (thesis · evidence · invalidation) is filed on entry. <0>Stop-loss required</0>; take-profit is optional and may be split into up to 3 rungs, each closing part of the position; the stop can also trail the price. Leverage inside your range, new-position margin under your cap; limit price within 5% of mark. The receipt carries the round-trip fee, stop distance and risk as % of equity, plus reward-to-risk after fees when a take-profit is set.
desc.close_position: Close all or part of a position at market, with a one-line reason.
desc.set_stop_loss: <0>Tighten only</0>: long stops move up, short stops move down. Reason required; goes into the public plan revision history. It can also start a trailing stop: given a callback percent, the platform follows the price and keeps moving the stop in the favourable direction only, without waking it.
desc.set_take_profit: Replaces the whole set of take-profit orders: up to 3 rungs, each a price plus the percent of the position it closes; they may move nearer, farther, or be removed. <0>Every rung must stay on the profit side of the current price</0>; to leave right now it has to close.
desc.write_plan: Only for a position with no plan on record; plans are immutable — a new thesis means adding or re-opening.
desc.set_watch: Watch conditions on one coin: price touches a level, a candle of some period closes above or below it, or a set time arrives. It is woken the moment one is met; at most one upward, one downward and one timed per coin, each fires once. Any coin the platform tracks can be watched, not only the tradable ones. A condition may also carry a standing order: when it fires the platform itself moves a stop, closes part or all of a position, or cancels a pending order — <0>risk-reducing only, never an entry</0>.
desc.get_account: Balance / positions / pending orders. Already injected every round; normally only called to re-check after its own orders.
desc.klines: 192 raw OHLCV bars, last one still forming. For bar-by-bar pattern checks or its own swing rules.
desc.kline_structure: Swings, segments, volume-by-price and key levels of the same bars; facts only, no calls. The leg-by-leg detail between swings comes only when it asks for it.
desc.indicators: MA/EMA · RSI · MACD · BOLL · ATR · KDJ · ADX · OBV · volume ratio, as of the last closed bar.
desc.market_snapshot: The latest raw reading from each data source: price change, funding rate, open interest, account and top-trader long/short ratios, taker volume, liquidations over the last 5 / 30 minutes, top-5 book depth, recent trades, fear & greed. No scoring.
desc.funding_history: Last 30 settlements plus next funding time and mark price.
desc.orderbook_depth: Top 10 bid/ask levels — where the walls sit.
desc.option_iv: Deribit DVOL and ATM implied volatility.
desc.derivatives_history: How Binance perp open interest, account long/short ratio, top-trader positioning and taker buy/sell ratio moved over the last 30 points.
desc.whale_positions: Hyperliquid on-chain whale positions, entries and liquidation levels, refreshed every 10 minutes; BTC / ETH / SOL / XRP / DOGE only.
desc.news_search: Recent market news flashes, full text; it can also search the local archive by keyword and time window (up to 7 days back).
desc.cross_asset_snapshot: Latest quotes and moves of US indices and index futures, the dollar index, the 10Y yield, VIX, gold and crude.
desc.web_search: One web search, returning a summary written from the results with source links. Only there when the model endpoint has web search on; each search costs one more model request.

model.intro: One endpoint = protocol + base URL + API key + model (+ reasoning effort). Chat, the trader and the review coach all pick from here; anything unbound uses the default — with a single endpoint that is your global config. To run different models off one key, add several.
model.empty: No endpoints yet — add one and chat / trader / review coach are all set

model.firstIsDefault: The first one becomes the default automatically

model.subAgentIntro: In the analysis chat, the main model can hand read-heavy work — research (news flashes + web) or market analysis — to background sub-agents that run in parallel, then follow up once their reports come back. Sub-agents run on the Chat · Light model and burn your own quota.

model.subAgentLimitHint: Cap on background tasks running at the same time (1–{{max}}); anything beyond is refused and the main model does it itself

endpoint.effortHint: Blank = the parameter is not sent and the model uses its own default; you can also enter any other level it accepts (xhigh, minimal…). Not every model accepts this, and there is no way to check up front — fill it in and hit Test connection.
endpoint.contextWindowHint: When this endpoint is the workbench chat's main model and context usage reaches 90% of this window, the context is compacted before the next turn starts. About 80% of the model's actual window works best: usage keeps growing within a turn, and compaction itself needs room. Range 128K–1000K (1M).
endpoint.webSearchHint: Declares this protocol's server-side search tool in requests. Saving and the connectivity test probe it first and block the endpoint if the upstream doesn't support it — untick it then. Only the workbench chat's main model and its research sub-agent use it — the trader and the market-analysis sub-agent are unaffected. Searches count toward upstream usage.

endpoint.antigravityHint: Antigravity won't take web search and local tools in the same request. When ticked, the model gets a local web search tool instead: each call sends a separate search-only request and hands the results back to the model. Leave it unticked for Google's official Gemini API.
